title: Adverbial clauses
prior_teaching_boundary: Only actual reviewed Units1–10 form, sense and construction milestones count. Prior supplied temporal connections, purpose clauses and source forms require explicit promotion or local support. Preserve every earlier identity, analysis and history.
productive_outcomes: Identify temporal, causal, purpose, result, concessive and conditional clause relations, distinguishing them from content clauses and relatives and from homographic adverbs or determiners.
Use the selected past and recurring when/then correlations, simultaneous while connections and anticipated before/until constructions with contextual mood choices and ordinary word-order tendencies.
Distinguish intended purpose, intended prevention and asserted result; use finite clauses with their own expressed subjects and contrast the earlier same-subject purpose infinitive.
Use the selected factual causal and concessive frames, and distinguish an open condition from an explicitly contrary-present condition without mechanically assigning mood from a conjunction.
Use complete assigned nominal, adjectival and verbal systems, including the new vowel, h-loss, syncope and consonant subpatterns, with their endings, important variants and lexical limits together.

Use explicitly assigned additional lexical and case frames required by all three Cook sets; distinguish each new productive sense or construction from familiar morphology and locally supplied expressions.

Complete all46 unchanged Cook IV.16–17 and V.18 prompts and the contracted original practice; read the connected new account independently and both exact source extracts with their printed local support.
recognition_outcomes: Recognize documented variants and reference-only nominal/adjectival cells without inferring new senses or syntax from complete morphological display.
Interpret the exact source participial periphrases, lexical variants and larger constructions through bounded help; do not impose a mechanical English progressive or perfect system.
Distinguish genuine source forms and original apparatus from declared formatting normalization and new teaching material.
bounded_scope: The actual ten-unit baseline alone establishes prior teaching.
Factual results use their audited indicative pattern; Cook’s optative curse is not a universal result-mood rule.
Concession can concede an admitted fact; gif does not automatically require subjunctive.
Only bounded anticipated before/until and explicitly contrary-present conditions are newly assigned. Broad tense sequence and past-counterfactual systems remain later work.
Complete base participle pairs do not assign unlisted adjective declensions, compound tenses or source periphrases.
Recognition number counterparts, adjective instrumental reference cells and exact supplied source spellings remain separately scoped.
The conventional singular moon is a lexical referential scope, not a mass-noun classification.
Both source spans remain exact, including the punctuation-only Bede dash, all original notes and the referenced earlier periphrasis note.
Source aids remain visible during supported tasks and never become unaided-recall targets.

audited_inflection_rules.description: Complete NGDA noun patterns use the cited Cook class models with each lexical stem. Mass/abstract plural reference cells do not establish new count senses.

Bæð keeps æ in singular and has a in plural baðu/baða/baðum; geat keeps ea in singular and has a in plural gatu/gata/gatum; sīðfæt has sīðfatas/sīðfata/sīðfatum. The changes belong to these checked lexemes, not all written vowels.
Seolh loses h and lengthens eo before case endings: sēol-. Bare nominative/accusative singular retain seolh. This completes a newly used subpattern.
Selected seolfor/frōfor/ceaster/winter use seolfr-/frōfr-/ceastr-/wintr- before endings. Īsern retains its medial e because the second syllable ends in rn; sumer retains its medial vowel.

Sumer and winter retain complete ordinary masculine systems; Cook43.5 also records occasional genitive/dative singular and nominative plural -a. The variants are accepted, not separately tested recall.

All ordinary adjective NGDA cells are productive; distinct instrumental masculine/neuter singular cells remain recognition reference. Blæc changes æ to a before vowel endings; consonantal endings retain æ. The weak genitive plural likewise retains æ before the shared strong ending -ra: blæcra in every gender. Stille/smylte retain final e only where no ending replaces it. Stille simplifies ll before consonantal endings: stilne/stilre/stilra, but stille/stilles/stillum.

The selected complete fæger, gesyndig and ðurstig tables retain the medial vowel. Cook57.3 also licenses syncope and occasional endingless feminine singular/neuter plural; the exact source gesyndge remains a separately supported syncopated realization. Fæger has independently attested retained and syncopated forms.

Dēorwierðra and fægerra are weak throughout, including predicates. Remove final e of dēorwierðe before -ra. Fægerra/fægerre are directly documented by BT264a. Genitive plurals dēorwierðra/fægerra apply the already taught consonant reduction; these full paradigms are rule-derived, not verbatim source tables.

local_support.learner_help: The preceding context concerns Britain, the island: hit refers to it. Swilce ... ēac, also. local_support.learner_help: Man is the impersonal singular subject “one”; dēð is third singular present indicative. Hine refers to the masculine stone. The newly taught placement frame dōn + object + on with accusative gives “puts it on/in a fire”; ðonne correlates with the gif condition.

source_spans.exact_text_without_note_cues:
Ðā wæs æfter langum fæce ðæt wē ūre gesihð feorr ūpāhōfon, ðā gesāwon wē in Farne, ðǣm īglande, Gode ðone lēofan fæder Æðelwald of his dīegelnessum ūtgangende, ðæt hē wolde ūrne sīðfæt scēawian, and gesēon hwæt ūs gelumpe, for-ðon hē gehīerde ðæt gebrec ðǣra storma and ðæs weallendes sǣs.

Mid-ðȳ hē ðā ūs ēac scēawode, and geseah in gewinne and in ōrmōdnesse gesętte bēon, ðā biegde hē his cnēowu tō Fæder ūres Dryhtnes Hǣlendes Crīstes, and wæs gebiddende for ūre hǣle and for ūrum līfe. And mid-ðȳ hē ðā ðæt gebed gefylde, hē ðā samod ætgædere ge ðone āðundnan sǣ gesmylte ge ðone storm gestilde, tō ðon ðætte ðurh eall sēo rēðnes ðæs stormes wæs blinnende, and gesyndge windas ðurh ðone smyltestan sǣ ūs æt lande gebrōhton. Mid-ðȳ wē ðā ūp cōmon tō lande, and ūre scip ēac swilce fram ðǣm ȳðum ūp ābǣron, ðā sōna se ilca storm ęft hwearf and cōm, se-ðe for ūrum intingan medmicel fæc gestilde, and ealne ðone dæg swīðe micel and strang wæs, ðætte męnn sweotollice ongietan meahton ðætte se medmicla fierst ðǣre stilnesse, ðe ðǣr becōm, tō bēnum ðæs Godes weres for intingan ūre hǣle heofonlice forgiefen wæs.

Ðā wæs æfter langum fæce ðæt wē ūre gesihð feorr ūpāhōfon, ðā gesāwon wē in Farne, ðǣm īglande, Gode ðone lēofan fæder Æðelwald of his dīegelnessum ūtgangende, ðæt hē wolde ūrne sīðfæt scēawian, and gesēon hwæt ūs gelumpe, for-ðon hē gehīerde ðæt gebrec ðǣra storma and ðæs weallendes sǣs.

Mid-ðȳ hē ðā ūs ēac scēawode, and geseah in gewinne and in ōrmōdnesse gesętte bēon, ðā biegde hē his cnēowu tō Fæder ūres Dryhtnes Hǣlendes Crīstes, and wæs gebiddende for ūre hǣle and for ūrum līfe. And mid-ðȳ hē ðā ðæt gebed gefylde, hē ðā samod ætgædere ge ðone āðundnan sǣ gesmylte ge ðone storm gestilde, tō ðon ðætte ðurh eall sēo rēðnes ðæs stormes wæs blinnende, and gesyndge windas ðurh ðone smyltestan sǣ ūs æt lande gebrōhton. Mid-ðȳ wē ðā ūp cōmon tō lande, and ūre scip ēac swilce fram ðǣm ȳðum ūp ābǣron, ðā sōna se ilca storm ęft hwearf and cōm, se-ðe for ūrum intingan medmicel fæc gestilde, and ealne ðone dæg swīðe micel and strang wæs, ðætte męnn sweotollice ongietan meahton ðætte se medmicla fierst ðǣre stilnesse, ðe ðǣr becōm, tō bēnum ðæs Godes weres for intingan ūre hǣle heofonlice forgiefen wæs.

new_material_examples.text: Ðā se fiscere cōm, ðā sæt se sunu on ðǣm hūse.
new_material_examples.translation: When the fisherman came, the son was sitting in the house.

new_material_examples.text: Ðā-hwīle-ðe se munuc sang, se sunu dranc wæter.
new_material_examples.translation: While the monk sang, the son drank water.

new_material_examples.text: Mid-ðȳ se sunu ǣt, se fæder sæt on ðǣm hūse.
new_material_examples.translation: While the son ate, the father sat in the house.

new_material_examples.text: Ne farað, ǣr se munuc cume.
new_material_examples.translation: Do not go before the monk comes.
new_material_examples.target: Plural command and an anticipated coming.
Singular command and an anticipated plural coming.

new_material_examples.text: Se mann healp ðǣm cuman, for-ðon-ðe hē wæs untrum.
new_material_examples.translation: The man helped the stranger because the stranger was sick.
new_material_examples.target: Factual cause; hē is explicitly taken to refer to the stranger in this example.

new_material_examples.text: Ic cume, ðæt ic ðē helpe.
new_material_examples.translation: I come so that I may help you.
new_material_examples.target: Present purpose with its own finite verb.

analysis.source_analysis: introduces a supplied finite content clause

new_material_examples.text: Se fæder cōm, ðæt hē his suna hulpe.
new_material_examples.translation: The father came so that he might help his son.

analysis.source_analysis: introduces a supplied finite content clause

new_material_examples.text: Heald ðæt dēor, ðȳ-lǣs-ðe hit ðone męte nime.
new_material_examples.translation: Hold the animal, lest it take the food.
new_material_examples.target: Intended prevention, not an extra negative in the main command.

new_material_examples.text: Se sunu wæs swā glæd, ðæt hē sang.
new_material_examples.translation: The son was so glad that he sang.

analysis.source_analysis: introduces a supplied finite content clause

new_material_examples.text: Ðēah se fiscere sīe eald, hē hilpð his suna.
new_material_examples.translation: Although the fisherman is old, he helps his son.

new_material_examples.text: Gif se munuc is hēr, hē hilpð ðǣm męnn.
new_material_examples.translation: If the monk is here, he helps the man.
new_material_examples.target: Open condition; the speaker does not know whether he is here.

new_material_examples.text: Gif se munuc wǣre hēr, hē hulpe ðǣm męnn.
new_material_examples.translation: If the monk were here, he would help the man.
new_material_examples.target: Contrary-present condition; the monk is absent now.

new_compositions.title: The fisherman and his son
new_compositions.text: Se ealda fiscere cōm tō ðǣm hūse, ðæt hē his suna hulpe. Ðā hē cōm, ðā wæs se sunu hungrig. Se fiscere sealde him męte. Mid-ðȳ se sunu ǣt, se fiscere bær wæter. Ðēah se fiscere wǣre eald, hē healp his suna. Se sunu cwæð: “Wes hēr, oð-ðæt ic cume.” Hē gewāt and cōm and sealde his fæder wæter.
new_compositions.target: A father helps his hungry son; the son responds with a promise to return and gives his father water. Purpose, past correlation, simultaneity, factual concession and anticipated until are explicit.
new_compositions.support_policy: All required forms, senses and constructions must be productive before this independent reading. No private full translation appears in this public seed.

grammar_inventory.description: Both directly addressed gewītan commands.
Past factual ðā-clause with indicative, optionally correlated with main-clause ðā then.
Recurring/future temporal ðonne-clause, optionally correlated with main-clause ðonne then; not a blanket subjunctive rule.
Factual simultaneous events with indicative; the spelling identifies a conjunction phrase.
Temporal clause, including factual past narration; distinguish the lexicalized conjunction from a freely parsed means phrase.
Selected anticipated event after a command with subjunctive; past factual before may also use subjunctive viewpoint. No indicative-only/future-only generalization.
Selected anticipated endpoint with subjunctive; no universal tense-sequence doctrine.
Purpose of prevention with subjunctive; negative meaning belongs to this conjunction and is not an instruction to negate the main clause.
Normally subjunctive, including admitted facts; subjunctive alone does not mean uncertainty.
Adversative coordination of clauses or parallel predicates; no subordinating mood requirement.
Through+accusative, literal spatial path; selected þ spelling is independently evidenced in Fulk199; Cook exact ðurh stays separately recorded.
Accusative opponent with feohtan; not the modern English accompaniment use of with.
rīsan ūp, rise up; opposition supplied by ongēan+accusative, not by ūp alone.
Besides+ dative in the assigned counting exclusion; does not teach every sense of būtan.
Factual cause with for-ðon-ðe; prior for-ðām retained.
Purpose ðæt with subjunctive; present and past examples bounded to the given contexts.

grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded Cook18.7 frame, distinct from direct-question hwonne and ordinary nominal relative roles.

grammar_inventory.description: Adverb mā with ðonne comparing amounts of doing; repeated predicate may be explicit or omitted.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Cook18.13 bounded verbal comparison; not merely prior copular adjective comparison.

grammar_inventory.scope_note: Selected factual indicative comparison in Cook18.5; distinguish adverb swā so and other source conjunction senses.

grammar_inventory.description: Bare strong genitive plurals dēadra/cwicra denote dead/living persons.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No article in the assigned construction; distinct from earlier article+weak personal adjectives.

grammar_inventory.description: Article plus weak rihtwīs/unrihtwīs denotes righteous/unrighteous people.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Explicitly extends the prior selected personal-adjective construction to rihtwīs; no assumption that familiar adjectival morphology already taught every personal sense.

grammar_inventory.description: Bounded nālæs hōlunga: not at all in vain, denying that the stated fighting was fruitless.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Selected emphatic negative-adverb phrase. Do not mechanically require an additional ne; no general negative-concord system or unrestricted nālæs syntax is taught.

grammar_inventory.description: Substantival eall: ealle all people (masculine plural) or eall everything (neuter singular).
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Cook16.13 permits either bounded interpretation if the number/meaning is stated; independent unspecified all is not a new noun paradigm.

grammar_inventory.description: Weak personal adjective used alone in singular direct address: lēofosta/lēofoste dearest.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Gender of addressee must be stated or a defensible alternative accepted; extends prior adjective+noun vocative to the bare adjective.

grammar_inventory.scope_note: Reuses actual u07-predicate-participle-variants; full participial adjective declensions and new plural cells are not implied.

grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded parenthetic request; no general object or clause-complement system for biddan is inferred.

grammar_inventory.description: Supplied nis in Cook17.12 and supplied ne sindon in the negative plural passive of Cook17.5.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Nis is an exact listed contraction. Ne sindon is declared local composition from Cook sindon and Fulk ne-before-verb; Fulk199 line60 independently attests ne sindan. No full negative wesan paradigm or independent uncontracted ne is production.

grammar_inventory.description: The preceding context concerns Britain, the island: hit refers to it. Swilce ... ēac, also. Berende on, rich in / productive of; węcga is genitive plural “of metals,” and ōrum dative plural “veins/ores” after on. The following genitives name the metals. Āres is Cook’s source spelling for copper here, beside the earlier selected ǣr.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Gemētt, found, is the exact past participle of prefixed gemētan; bið gemētt, is found. Gagates is jet, the stone’s Latin loan-name; stān, stone, masculine nominative singular. The second bið links stone with black gem.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Man is the impersonal singular subject “one”; dēð is third singular present indicative. Hine refers to the masculine stone. The newly taught placement frame dōn + object + on with accusative gives “puts it on/in a fire”; ðonne correlates with the gif condition.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Flēoð is third plural present indicative of flēon, flee; it is not the verb fly. Ðǣr, there; næddran, snakes/adders, nominative plural of weak feminine næddre; onwęg, away. Both d letters in næddran belong to the printed text.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Read the whole opening as “then, after a long time, it happened that ...”. Æfter governs the dative; langum fæce means a long interval. The opening ðæt belongs to this supplied time-introduction frame.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Gesihð is feminine accusative singular, sight/gaze; ūre agrees with it. Feorr, far off. Ūpāhōfon, we lifted up, first plural preterite of ūpāhebban. The complete phrase describes looking up and seeing at a distance.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: In Farne, on Farne island, with ðǣm īglande as dative apposition. Gode ðone lēofan fæder means the father dear to God: the adjective’s complement is dative. Æðelwald is in apposition to the accusative fæder. Of + dative means out of/from; dīegelnessum is the source plural for retreat/seclusion. Ūtgangende is the printed participle, coming out; Cook notes that a present participle is used for a Latin past participle here, so “having come out” is also possible.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: The ðæt clause gives his purpose. Wolde with the infinitives scēawian and gesēon is read here “that he might watch and see” or “in order to watch and see”; do not make private desire the only force. Hwæt ūs gelumpe is a dependent question, what might happen to us. Gelumpe is third singular preterite subjunctive, and ūs is dative.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: For-ðon is the shorter source spelling of the causal conjunction. Gehīerde, heard, is a prefixed past form. Gebrec is the accusative noise/crash; ðǣra storma is genitive plural of storms, and ðæs weallendes sǣs genitive singular of the surging sea. Weallendes is an adjectival participle, surging/boiling. Ðǣra preserves the source genitive-plural spelling.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: The temporal clause contains both scēawode and geseah. With geseah, understand the earlier ūs as the people seen: he saw us to be situated in distress and despair. In governs the two datives gewinne and ōrmōdnesse. Gesętte is plural past participle here, not the identically spelled finite past; bēon is infinitive. This entire perception complement is supplied.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Biegde, bent, is the exact third singular preterite spelling; cnēowu, knees, accusative plural. Tō Fæder marks the direction of the prayer. Ūres Dryhtnes Hǣlendes Crīstes is a genitive group: of our Lord Jesus Christ, with the proper title Hǣlend and Crīst in apposition.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Cook143 note1 refers to142 note7: this was + participle wording is read as a simple past here, “prayed.” Do not infer a universal English progressive rule. For ūre hǣle, for our safety/rescue, uses accusative; for ūrum līfe, for our life, uses dative. Keep both exact constructions supplied.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Gebed is prayer, accusative singular; gefylde is the already taught finished/accomplished. Samod ætgædere means together/at once. Paired ge ... ge coordinates both ... and; the first ge introduces the sea-calming and the second the storm-stilling.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Āðundnan, swollen, is a weak participial adjective agreeing with masculine accusative sǣ. Gesmylte, calmed, is third singular preterite; storm is accusative singular. Gestilde retains the taught transitive quell/settle sense here.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Tō ðon ðætte introduces the result, so that. Ðurh eall is the exact adverbial expression completely/entirely. Rēðnes, fury, is the feminine subject; ðæs stormes is genitive. Wæs blinnende is the supplied periphrasis “ceased” here, with present participle blinnende; no new productive progressive tense is introduced.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Gesyndge is the exact syncopated source form beside taught gesyndige, favorable, nominative plural. Smyltestan is the weak masculine accusative superlative calmest/very calm. Ðurh governs ðone ... sǣ; ūs is the accusative people brought. Æt lande means to/at land in this exact arrival expression. Gebrōhton is the prefixed third plural preterite brought.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: The temporal clause has the two completed actions: we came up onto land and carried our ship up from the waves. Lande is the locally supplied dative of land; ȳðum is dative plural waves after fram. Ābǣron is first plural preterite of prefixed carry. Ūre scip is the accusative object, not a new subject.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Sōna, immediately; ęft, again; hwearf, returned. Se-ðe is the exact relative complex referring to masculine storm. For ūrum intingan, for our sake; intingan is dative singular. Medmicel fæc is accusative duration, a short interval. Gestilde is intransitive ceased/became still in this relative clause; the earlier transitive sense alone is insufficient. English had ceased may clarify the sequence.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Ealne ðone dæg is accusative duration, all that day. Strang, strong, agrees with storm. The first ðætte introduces the result: people could clearly understand. Sweotollice, clearly; ongietan, understand, is the infinitive governed by meahton. The second ðætte introduces what they understand, a content clause.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Fierst is masculine nominative singular, interval/period; medmicla is its weak adjective, short. Ðǣre stilnesse, of the calm, is genitive singular. In the relative clause, ðǣr means there and becōm means occurred/came about in this context.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Tō bēnum, at/in response to the prayers, uses dative plural. Ðæs Godes weres means of the man of God; weres is genitive singular, with Godes depending on it. For intingan ūre hǣle means for the sake of our rescue: hǣle is genitive singular; exact ūre is supplied in this possessive expression. Heofonlice means from heaven; forgiefen means given/granted here, expressly not forgiven. The final passive refers to the brief period of calm.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Bounded exact source expression; full source help remains visible for all assigned analysis/translation tasks. This record does not license independent production of its untaught parts.

grammar_inventory.description: For Cook17.17 supply the entire fēower ðūsend manna phrase, four thousand men, with genitive group after the higher numeral.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Adapted local phrase using checked higher numeral and Cook154c genitive relation; no general higher-numeral production system.

grammar_inventory.description: Nouns naming the same referent in apposition take the same case. In the assigned title/name phrase Dryhtnes Hǣlendes Crīstes all three are genitive singular; appositional God and Fæder retain their nominative role in the blessing.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Cook151 case agreement, bounded to ordinary title/name and identifying noun apposition. Earlier source-only appositions retain their histories. Existing genitive dependencies and possessive agreement remain separate.

actual_prior_record.scope_note: The lexical sense is distinct from any still-supplied source construction.
Productive both lexical use. Formal unassigned number counterparts do not add new senses.
Weak adjective used as a personal substantive, as explicitly taught for the assigned Cook prompts; ordinary adjective sense stays separately identified.

actual_prior_record.gloss: be as an auxiliary with the selected passive participle
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Does not change the earlier ordinary copular sense or teach every perfect/progressive construction.
Productive both lexical use. Formal unassigned number counterparts do not add new senses.
Complete present/preterite indicative morphology; elementary lexical frame separately evidenced. No subjunctive, passive, conditional or unattested nonfinite system.
Ordinary noun senses and prior subject, object, limiting-genitive and explicitly taught prepositional uses only. Does not establish new government, quantifiers or source-only idioms.
Complete present/preterite indicative morphology; elementary lexical frame separately evidenced. No subjunctive, passive, conditional or unattested nonfinite system.
Complete NGDA singular/plural morphology; plural reference cells do not assign an unneeded mass/abstract number sense.

actual_prior_record.description: Produce the selected article forms agreeing with their own noun in gender, number and nominative/genitive/dative/accusative case.
Produce every person/number cell of the present eom/eart/is/sindon and preterite wæs/wǣre/wæs/wǣron indicative series.
Use a dative recipient and accusative thing given in the explicitly supplied sealde frame; distinguish to/for-recipient from the direct object.
Use fram plus dative for the entity from which something is separated, in an explicitly supplied separating frame.
Produce limiting relational genitives. Follow Cook's exercise target: dependent first, head noun without its own article; retain the dependent's required article.
Preserve the head's externally governed case while its own limiting dependent remains genitive; the genitive article belongs to that dependent.
Coordinate nominal phrases with and; each article agrees with its own head.
Use taught locative on with dative ('in/on'); this is a selected construction, not a universal spatial rule.
Use the copula's appropriate number/person in the taught ordinary clauses.
Finite subjects and noun predicates identifying the subject are nominative; ordinary bare noun predicates need no translated indefinite article.
Ordinary independent active clauses: nominative subject, finite person/number agreement. Exercise order is a model, not a universal mandatory rule.
Coordinate simple clauses/predicates with and, allowing the same subject to remain understood in the second finite predicate of the stated examples.
Subject+sęcgan introduces a direct independent utterance with colon/quotation marks. Quoted pronouns belong to its speaker; no indirect complement syntax.
Independently formed sęllan: dative recipient, accusative thing, noun/pronoun arguments. No sęndan recipient government inferred.
Use nominative subjects and governed object/recipient cases; grammatical gender/number tracks referents, including inanimate nouns. Syncretic spelling alone does not settle antecedence.
his/hiere/hiera are invariant possessors; possessor reference determines choice, while the head keeps its own case/number.
Selected adverbs qualify actions or whole statements without case/number/gender agreement; sōðlice truly is distinct from the supplied source connective sense.
glæd alternates æ/a in its checked cells; this is not an unrestricted substitution rule.
Adjectives agree with their own noun/referent in case, number and gender; attributive and ordinary positive predicate uses are taught.
Cardinal one with singular nouns, 2–12 with plural count nouns; numeral gender/case agrees where the selected system inflects.
Checked cardinal 4–12 forms used invariantly before plural count nouns; no postposed/substantival inflection or higher-number partitive syntax.
Comparatives are weak attributively and predicatively; full paradigms include transparently derived genitive plural contractions and licensed -ena selections.
Bounded subject A + copula + comparative + ðonne + parallel subject B: B is nominative, with repeated copula understood. No generalized comparative-clause or genitive-standard syntax.
eald/ieldra/ieldest is the assigned umlaut series; no universal umlaut instruction.

Ordinary attributive adjectives are weak after article/demonstrative; bare ordinary adjectives are strong. After possessives Cook permits strong and sometimes weak; no universal possessive→weak rule and no new rule for adjectives after limiting genitives.
Existing se/sēo/ðæt morphology now also expresses pointing that/those; relative and general third-person pronoun uses remain unassigned.
Long adjective stems: zero feminine nominative singular and neuter N/A plural in selected monosyllabic strong paradigms.
Complete ðes/ðēos/ðis system: this/these, agreeing with the noun in N/G/D/A; reference instrumentals do not create syntax milestones.
The six agreeing possessives have complete strong morphology. Their endings agree with the possessed noun, not the possessor; personal-genitive citations retain separate records.
Ordinary positive predicative adjectives are strong and nominative, agreeing with the subject even when its noun phrase contains an article. Comparatives remain weak.
Complete selected weak N/G/D/A singular/plural; ordinary genitive plural -ra and explicitly audited comparative exceptions.
Selected ordinary transitive uses: drīfan drives cattle, bindan binds an animal, cēosan chooses a thing, findan finds a thing and drincan drinks water; the direct object is accusative.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Exact lexical government is independently evidenced. Cattle, an animal, ships and dwellings in these new compositions are declared ordinary lexical applications, not falsely attributed source quotations. No universal strong-verb accusative rule.

actual_prior_record.description: Helpan takes the dative being or recipient helped in the selected ordinary use. The attested person examples support the declared new application to birds.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Dative being/recipient is the selected target. Attested human examples support the explicitly declared ordinary lexical application to birds. The documented genitive alternative is valid but is not the construction requested here.

actual_prior_record.description: Rīdan ride and singan sing may stand without a nominal object; prior manner adverbs qualify the action.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No directional complement or instrumental transport is implied by riding.

actual_prior_record.description: Flēogan fly, scīnan shine, swimman swim and weaxan grow have their independently checked ordinary intransitive uses.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Bird, star, fish and tree subjects follow the exact Cook prompts; spatial on+dative can locate the swimming without adding direction.

actual_prior_record.description: Beran in carry and niman in take have an accusative person/thing as their selected ordinary object.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: The new food/fish examples are declared ordinary lexical applications, not falsely attributed source quotations; no goal or source preposition is introduced.

actual_prior_record.description: Cweðan introduces direct quoted speech with an independent finite clause; quoted first-person reference belongs to the quoted speaker.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Explicit extension of the earlier sęcgan quotation frame; content clauses, reported speech and requests remain outside production.

actual_prior_record.description: Etan means eat, with an accusative food object or with the food understood in an ordinary objectless use.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No partitive genitive, infinitive complement or idiom of consuming something figuratively is assigned.

actual_prior_record.description: Sittan, licgan and standan describe ordinary intransitive posture; a previously taught locative on+dative phrase may locate the subject.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No causal placement, directional complement or stand-against construction is inferred.

actual_prior_record.description: Slēan strike and healdan hold take an accusative person/thing in their selected ordinary physical senses.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No instrumental means, command, maintaining-state complement or additional sense is inferred.

actual_prior_record.description: Cuman means come in an ordinary intransitive clause and supplies the movement verb before the selected same-subject purpose infinitive.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No unassigned destination phrase or sense of becuman follows.

actual_prior_record.description: The prior cweðan direct-quotation frame now also introduces the independently taught second-person commands. Quoted reference belongs to the speaker/addressee context.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Only the expressly selected forms, senses and constructions are assigned.

actual_prior_record.description: Dōn means do/perform with an accusative work/thing in the selected elementary clauses, complements and commands.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No causative, passive, perfect or arbitrary phrasal sense.

actual_prior_record.description: Faran means go/travel in an ordinary intransitive clause and as the action in the newly taught volitional complement.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No destination, vehicle, motion-preposition or sailing sense is implied.

actual_prior_record.description: Ne directly precedes the selected negative imperative in the taught prohibition.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No general claim that every Old English prohibition must have imperative morphology.

actual_prior_record.description: Second-singular commands address one person; plural commands address two or more, without a separate dual ending. The subject can remain unexpressed in the selected direct instructions.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: These are second-person commands, not third-person optative wishes or a new general politeness system.

actual_prior_record.description: Selected plain and inflected infinitive forms, including weak -ian, j-present and contracted/anomalous stems; productive inflected targets use the explicitly selected -anne series with stated variants.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Earlier citations gain new scope only by exact form assignment. Participles remain supplied; no unattested modal infinitive is generated.

actual_prior_record.description: The selected infinitives retain their audited lexical argument relations: carrying/taking/eating have accusative objects, helping a dative person, and giving an accusative thing with dative recipient.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Only the expressly selected forms, senses and constructions are assigned.

actual_prior_record.description: The finite modal/volitional verb carries subject agreement; its selected plain infinitive does not acquire person/number endings or tō in the taught construction.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Only the expressly selected forms, senses and constructions are assigned.

actual_prior_record.description: Elementary purpose after cuman is expressed with tō plus the selected inflected infinitive; the understood actor is the person/people who come.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No general purpose-clause subjunctive, indirect command, arbitrary controller or other infinitival construction.

actual_prior_record.description: Willan plus a plain infinitive expresses desire or willingness; wolde can state past desire without asserting that the desired act occurred.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Only the expressly selected forms, senses and constructions are assigned.

actual_prior_record.description: Open gif clauses can use indicative. A contextually tentative/hypothetical request can use present subjunctive, followed by an imperative or ordinary indicative main clause. Gif itself never licenses an automatic conversion rule.

For assigned accusative-object verbs, present or preterite wesan/bēon or weorðan + past participle expresses passive. Finite auxiliary agrees with the nominative subject. Agent omitted in productive tasks; no new fram-agent rule needed. Wesan often presents state/result and weorðan event, but not an absolute contrast or one-to-one English tense mapping.
The learned second-person imperative or new present subjunctive of the auxiliary combines with the selected past participle to command or wish a passive situation. The participle is nonfinite.
In verbal predicates a past participle may be uninflected or take strong-masculine-like endings: neuter plural dēor bunden/bundene are both licensed. Attributive agreement remains a different target.

Spatial ofer permits the source-attested accusative/dative constructions. Fulk§36 explicitly verifies both governments; exact eorðan is syncretic, so its surface alone cannot prove either case. Authority ofer+accusative is separately taught. No unrestricted case interchange or exceptionless motion/rest rule is assigned.

Direct yes/no questions commonly begin with the finite verb; wh-words or phrases commonly precede the finite verb, and a wh-subject is itself the subject. No English dummy do is added. These are tendencies, not an exceptionless V2 transformation.

Ordinary attributive sum some/a certain, ǣnig any in questions, gehwilc each with singular noun, and swilc such; complete strong morphology. Following ordinary descriptive adjective in swilc phrases is strong. Extended negative/distributive/partitive/correlative constructions deferred.
Question pronouns take the case their own function requires: subject nominative, possessor genitive, object accusative, recipient or governed dative.

In selected productive relative clauses, gender and number track the antecedent while relative case is governed by its function within its own clause. An antecedent in dative can have a nominative relative, and vice versa; this is the selected ordinary construction, not a universal ban on attraction.
Invariant ðe introduces an ordinary relative clause and can represent different internal case functions; it is not an English personal interrogative pronoun.
A finite content clause introduced by invariant ðæt fills the content complement of the selected knowing/saying verb.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Keep distinct from determiner/relative ðæt; clause has its own subject and finite verb.

actual_prior_record.description: Sęcgan can name its recipient in the dative with direct speech or a dependent content/question complement.
Mid + dative names an accompanying person or cargo.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Means/manner/abstract circumstance require their own prior or supplied records.

actual_prior_record.description: Gesēon can take an accusative actor and a plain infinitive describing the perceived action.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: The actor belongs to the infinitival event; no claim that every verb takes this construction.

actual_prior_record.description: Use the nominative-shaped noun in direct address; an accompanying adjective is weak. Thus the morphology of the noun follows number and its own class, while good in O good fellows/workmen uses weak plural. Ēalā is an optional interjection where the original English says O.
actual_prior_record.prior_status: Only an exact merchant vocative was supplied in Unit8.

actual_prior_record.description: Gewītan means depart/go away and may take fram+dative source.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Not the distinct short-vowel preterite-present know.

actual_prior_record.description: Hwonne introduces a direct when-question using ordinary finite interrogative syntax.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No temporal subordinate when-clause system is introduced.

actual_prior_record.description: Use mid+dative for concrete means and distinguish it from accompaniment.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Prose-default selected pattern; no Anglian mid+distinct instrument production.

actual_prior_record.description: Present indicative can refer to future events where context supplies futurity; English will/shall need not produce willan.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Willan remains volitional where intention is meant; no new periphrastic future tense.

actual_prior_record.description: Scrȳdan clothes an accusative person.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Garment mid+dative is documented reference evidence only; it is not an additional independently assigned lexical complement.

actual_prior_record.description: Supplied sęllan +dative person +plain drincan: give someone to drink.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Local Cook III.14.11 support; not independent recall of a general purpose construction.

actual_prior_record.description: The selected weak adjectives with the article can name people: the hungry, naked, sick, unrighteous; case and number follow their clause role.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Plural people and an adjective modifying an expressed singular person must be distinguished. Do not imply every abstract substantive use is covered.

actual_prior_record.description: Tō+dative gives a destination with come/go/fly.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Separate from tō purpose/function and tō+inflected infinitive.

authoring_rules: Preserve every task/key identifier and Cook English prompt, control and reference. Keep the three complete source sets together; editorial directions and local helps remain separate from original wording.

Print complete new class/subpattern paradigms literally. Familiar-class derivations require actual printed complete models and explicit diagnostic stems and ending operations for every cell. Teach rules, exceptions and scope beside the tables.

Give contextual mood choices, not conjunction-to-mood transformations. Subjunctive need not mean false, factual result is normally indicative, and past morphology need not mean past time in a stated contrary-present setting.
Teach each required form, sense and lexical frame before independent use. Print all contracted local support at its point of use; no silent promotion of source-only, recognition or citation records.

Preserve both complete source spans and all original notes, including the explicitly cross-referenced participial note. Keep exact transcription, normalization, prior context and new teaching material distinguishable. Punctuation tokens do not become lexical records.
The controlled account and fourteen translated teaching examples are explicitly new composition. All actual inputs and required outputs need form/sense/construction bindings.

The separate key gives models, essential meaning, target explanation, defensible alternatives and useful error diagnoses. Grammatical validity and compliance with a stated target are distinct judgments.

The reserved independent reviewer solves every actual learner task before key/private-model access, freezes solutions and discloses prior grammar/public-evidence work. The reviewer edits only review files.

Resolve material findings before LuaLaTeX exports. Verify complete Markdown/TeX/PDF parity and every final page with a non-author. Integrate reviewed records while preserving every prior artifact and history; update README/status/handoff/source indexes, export Beads and commit locally. Do not draft Unit12.

lexical_frames.frame_and_boundary: Dative entity harmed. Selected weak-I system; strong scōd is outside the production system.
Accusative entity distinguished or adorned; mid+dative feature/equipment, with an agentless passive permitted.
Accusative event/person watched, including a journey; plain infinitive after volitional willan.
Intransitive fight; opponent introduced by wið+accusative. This is opposition, not accompaniment.
Dative person/place/event approached; includes time approaching an event. Selected -cte follows Cook113; attested -hte is a documented alternative.
Accusative thing hidden; agentless state/result passive with wesan.
Accusative person/thing brought; tō+dative destination/person. Selected weak preterite brōhte, not the separate strong variant.
Past factual ðā-clause with indicative, optionally correlated with main-clause ðā then.
Recurring/future temporal ðonne-clause, optionally correlated with main-clause ðonne then; not a blanket subjunctive rule.
Factual simultaneous events with indicative; the spelling identifies a conjunction phrase.
Temporal clause, including factual past narration; distinguish the lexicalized conjunction from a freely parsed means phrase.
Selected anticipated event after a command with subjunctive; past factual before may also use subjunctive viewpoint. No indicative-only/future-only generalization.
Selected anticipated endpoint with subjunctive; no universal tense-sequence doctrine.
Purpose of prevention with subjunctive; negative meaning belongs to this conjunction and is not an instruction to negate the main clause.
Normally subjunctive, including admitted facts; subjunctive alone does not mean uncertainty.
Adversative coordination of clauses or parallel predicates; no subordinating mood requirement.
Through+accusative, literal spatial path; selected þ spelling is independently evidenced in Fulk199; Cook exact ðurh stays separately recorded.
Accusative opponent with feohtan; not the modern English accompaniment use of with.
rīsan ūp, rise up; opposition supplied by ongēan+accusative, not by ūp alone.
Besides+ dative in the assigned counting exclusion; does not teach every sense of būtan.
Promotes actual earlier supplied then-adverb; distinguish from new past when-conjunction.
Promotes earlier supplied then sense for sequence/correlation; prior than-sense remains distinct.
Promotes earlier supplied factual causal conjunction; selected factual cause takes indicative.
Purpose with subjunctive, separate from previously taught content sense and new factual-result sense.
